evals.prompt: I already have a decent roleDetailDesc, but the welcome is flat: "Hello, I am your new mentor. What do you want to do?" Redesign the opening and first two turns so the first screen is immediately playable.
evals.expected_output: Produces an opening packet, replaces the greeting with a scene, defines reply paths, expected first user message, second-turn move, state change, token tradeoff, and handoff without MCP calls.
expectations: The output routes to lunatalk-opening-director or uses opening-design.md.
The diagnosis identifies greeting-only failure and missing place, role action, pressure, player implication, and reply path.
The welcome draft includes a concrete scene and clear player actions.
The second-turn move changes state, risk, relationship, route, or information.
The output does not call mutating MCP tools.

evals.prompt: My fantasy city card welcome explains all calendar districts for 900 words before the courier can act. Make the first screen playable without losing the core concept.
evals.expected_output: Moves lore out of welcome, opens on one delivery problem, exposes state or choices, defines first user message and second-turn consequence.
expectations: The output identifies lore-before-action and welcome bloat as the failure.
The opening keeps only the lore needed for the first action.
The player role, current pressure, and reply paths are clear.
The token tradeoff moves reusable rules into roleDetailDesc or Theme V3/XMLV3 state.
The self-review checks first reply speed and second-turn change.

evals.prompt: The ensemble welcome introduces all five crew members one by one and then asks what I do. Fix the opening so I can actually play.
evals.expected_output: Chooses one focal crisis, defines turn ownership, delays cast roll call, creates player implication, reply paths, and a second-turn move that changes group tension.
expectations: The output identifies ensemble roll call as the failure.
The opening starts with one focal speaker or crisis instead of every cast member.
The player can affect group tension through clear reply paths.
The second-turn move updates trust, risk, route, or cast conflict.
The handoff says whether authoring or simulation is next.

evals.prompt: The welcome is beautiful, but it tells the player they blush, obey, and follow the role into the next room. The choices are only mood labels. Fix the first screen.
evals.expected_output: Routes the agency failure through lunatalk-agency-designer or agency-design, then produces an opening packet with player insertion space, concrete reply paths, and second-turn consequences.
expectations: The output identifies player-feeling narration, forced action, and decorative choices as agency failures.
The repair uses or preserves an agency packet before polishing the welcome.
The welcome draft leaves identity, emotion, intention, method, and boundary choices to the player.
The reply paths change response, information, relationship, state, risk, route, or next hook.
The output does not call mutating MCP tools.
